outcome: Perinatal affective symptoms (prenatal depression, physio-somatic symptoms like fatigue, pain, dyspepsia, gastro-intestinal symptoms)
Mother outcome characteristics (hyperpigmentation, labor duration, caesarian section, cord length, breast milk flow)
Baby outcome characteristics (sleep and feeding problems)
cohort: The study included pregnant women with and without prenatal depression and non-pregnant controls.
finding: Increased oxidative & nitrosative stress at the end of term is associated with perinatal depressive and physio-somatic symptoms and predicts obstetric and behavioral complications in mother and baby.
mod_finding: Increased oxidative & nitrosative stress and lowered TRAP and PON1 activity at the end of term predict caesarian section as a mother outcome characteristic.
